subject: Full subsystem codebase scan for identifying pre-existing issues?

reviews.author: Derek Barbosa
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested marking pre-existing issues in the web UI more clearly by visually distinguishing them from new bugs, such as using bold text or a different font color.

reviewer noted that current pre-existing issue reporting could be improved by visually marking these issues differently in the web UI, suggesting bold text or different font colors to distinguish them from newly reported bugs

Reviewer suggested marking pre-existing issues as such in the web UI, either by prefacing them with a bold label or displaying them differently, to help distinguish between new and existing bugs.

Reviewer noted that Sashiko's pre-existing issue reporting may be less accurate due to differences in underlying LLMs and custom prompts used by various harnesses, and suggested visually marking pre-existing issues differently for better differentiation.

Reviewer suggested marking pre-existing issues in the Sashiko web UI more obviously, such as with a bold label or different font color, to help differentiate them from newly introduced bugs.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

On Thu, Jul 30, 2026 at 05:34:10PM -0700, Joanne Koong wrote:

---

We're actively working on trying to get more data (such as semcode) to act as
some sort of backing "evidence" of a finding. That, in theory, should at least
filter out the totally bogus claims. But it is still all a WIP.

---

I see what you mean. I think there may be a way to reach a "good enough"
solution in the interim: https://github.com/sashiko-dev/sashiko/issues/385

---

Right. From what I've seen, different harnesses (claude code, opencode,
gemini-cli, etc) have their own set of underlying prompts and housekeeping logic
that result in an interesting set of permutations when you throw custom prompts
and tool calls in the mix. Sashiko would be an example of a harness (one
tailored to work in a more "distributed" fashion) that calls out to Gemini in
the current "prod" instance).

FWIW I have also seen considerable differences in said prompts across different
harnesses, etc.

---

I'll take note of that and try to run an experiment or two with your
suggestions. Changing prompts can feel like alchemy at times! :)

2026-07-31.patch_summary: This patch proposes to modify the Sashiko tool's codebase scan to include pre-existing issues, allowing maintainers to identify and address them more easily. The idea is to visually mark these issues differently from new ones, making it easier for contributors to distinguish between bugs they caused and existing problems. This change aims to improve the overall efficiency of the review process.
